findings.title: Fix verification picks its test by scraping any pytest node id out of a finding's prose evidence, so a mis-scraped id that fails at HEAD force-reopens a correctly-resolved finding over the tester's judgment
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:273-274 - cited_tests() runs the regex _TEST_ID over every evidence string: `for line in finding.get("evidence") or []: ids += _TEST_ID.findall(str(line))`. Evidence is prose. Any node id quoted inside it - a code excerpt, a cross-reference to a different finding's test - is taken as this finding's demonstrating test.
src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:398 - only the first is ever used: `test_id = tests[0]`. Selection is therefore evidence ORDER, not relevance.

LIVE THIS RUN: facts.json verification.VERDICT-F-20 records test 't.py::new', at_previous 'error', at_head 'error'. There is no t.py in this repository. The id was scraped from F-20's own evidence line quoting a test's source: `assert facts["test_ids"]["added"] == ["t.py::new"]`. F-20 is genuinely fixed this run and could not be auto-verified because the harness ran a fabricated test.

PROVEN by counterfactual in a scratch two-commit git repo (tempfile dir, never the checkout), using the shipped collect() and merge(): a finding whose evidence[0] cross-references an unrelated still-failing test (`test_other.py::test_unrelated_known_failure`) and whose evidence[2] cites its own real test (`test_pkg.py::test_pending`). cited_tests returned ['test_other.py::test_unrelated_known_failure', 'test_pkg.py::test_pending'] - the cross-reference first.

PROVEN consequence, same probe: the defect WAS fixed (pkg.py q-i -> q+i) and the judgment said status 'resolved'. merge() returned status 'open', delta 'STILL_OPEN', resolution_refused 'test_other.py::test_unrelated_known_failure still fails at HEAD - measured by verdict-facts, so the resolution is not accepted'. A correct resolution was overturned by a measurement of an unrelated test.

src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:443-452 - _apply_verification applies this before the outcome is derived, and it overrides both an explicit `resolved` and silence, so the wrong STILL_OPEN also reaches outcomes.json as an undecided finding and depresses the calibration track record the agent contract (§9) says the model must not be able to influence.

The cross-check already exists and is not used: facts["_test_ids"] - the collected id set - is assigned at harness.py:871, two lines before verify_findings is called at harness.py:873, and is never passed in. An id absent from the collected set cannot be this suite's test.

tests/test_verification.py:261 test_cited_tests_reads_ids_not_line_references pins exactly the permissive behaviour: it asserts that an id inside the prose 'see tests/test_c.py::TestK::test_m: assert 1 == 2' IS returned. The suite guards the scrape rather than the selection, so nothing goes red on either failure mode.

root_cause.symptom: a finding the tester resolved is written to state as STILL_OPEN with a resolution_refused message naming a test that has nothing to do with it; separately, a genuinely fixed finding (F-20) is verified against a test id that does not exist
root_cause.mechanism: cited_tests() treats evidence prose as a citation index and _TEST_ID matches any `<path>.py::<name>` anywhere in it, including inside quoted source; verify_findings then takes tests[0], so the chosen test is whichever id appears earliest in the narrative; _apply_verification treats that test's HEAD result as authoritative over the tester's status
root_cause.origin: the feature landed whole in e71121a (v0.53.0, 'the loop closes - the harness verifies fixes') in this range; the permissiveness is deliberate at the extraction site (its test asserts it) and the risk was not carried through to the selection and override sites
root_cause.class: searched src/ for other consumers of cited_tests: verify_findings is the only one, and _apply_verification the only consumer of its record - so two sites, one pattern. The wider shape is 'a measurement derived from natural-language prose given authority over an explicit judgment', and this is currently its only instance.

evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:562 - `rc, db, out = qa_root / "coverage.rc", qa_root / "coverage.db", qa_root / "coverage.json"`. All three land in the QA root, which in team mode IS the committed .qa/ directory.
MEASURED THIS RUN: `ls -la .qa/coverage.*` -> coverage.json 94,987,311 bytes (95 MB), coverage.db 221,184 bytes, coverage.rc 279 bytes.

`git check-ignore -v .qa/coverage.db .qa/coverage.json .qa/coverage.rc` prints nothing and exits 1 - none of the three is ignored. `git status --porcelain` lists all three as untracked (`?? .qa/coverage.db`, `?? .qa/coverage.json`, `?? .qa/coverage.rc`).

.qa/.gitignore lists facts.json, judgment.json, state.json.prev and run-in-progress.json and states the policy in its own header: 'Per-run intermediates: the harness rewrites these every run ... What belongs in git is the record - state.json, the reports, the run history, the outcome ledger, the profile - not the scratch a single run passed through.' The three coverage files are exactly that scratch and were not added when diff coverage shipped in 6e6a859 (v0.54.0).
They are never removed. harness.py:566-567 does `db.unlink(missing_ok=True); out.unlink(missing_ok=True)` at the START of the next run only, so between runs the 95 MB file simply sits in the QA root.
profile.md:52-53 records that committing .qa/ is the maintainer's act and VERDICT-F-2 makes it necessary for the self-gate, so the commit that captures this is expected rather than hypothetical.
GitHub refuses any file over 100 MB on push; 95 MB is 5% under the wall and coverage.json scales with tests x changed lines, which grew 9.2% in test count in this range alone.

Second-order, same line: harness.py:591 reads the whole file with `json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`, so the render step also holds ~95 MB of JSON plus its parsed object in memory in one go.

root_cause.symptom: three untracked per-run intermediates, one of them 95 MB, sitting in a directory whose whole purpose is to be committed and shared
root_cause.mechanism: the QA root is used as scratch space for the coverage run (COVERAGE_FILE and the rendered JSON both point into it) while .qa/.gitignore enumerates intermediates by name, so a new intermediate is un-ignored by default; the `--show-contexts` JSON carries a per-line list of test contexts, which is what makes it two orders of magnitude larger than the database it came from

findings.title: Fix verification copies the cited test back to the old commit only when the whole test FILE is absent there, so a regression test appended to an existing test file yields at_previous 'error' and fix_verified is silently never set
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:407-412 - the copy-back is file-level and conditional on absence: `test_file = test_id.split("::", 1)[0]; src, dst = Path(repo) / test_file, scratch / test_file; if not dst.exists() and src.is_file(): ... shutil.copyfile(src, dst)`. When the file exists at the previous commit, the scratch checkout keeps the OLD file - which does not contain the newly added test function.

PROVEN by counterfactual in a scratch two-commit git repo (tempfile dir, never the checkout), using the shipped collect() and merge(): commit A has test_pkg.py containing only test_signature; commit B fixes pkg.py and APPENDS test_pending to the same file. Verification record: {"test": "test_pkg.py::test_pending", "at_previous": "error", "at_head": "pass", "summary": "(no match in any of [<Module test_pkg.py>]) -> 1 passed in 0.00s"}. merge() returned fix_verified: None on an explicit `resolved`.

The control is the shipped test's own scenario: tests/test_verification.py:129 test_a_test_the_fix_added_is_carried_back_to_the_old_commit builds the same repo with `bugged_repo(tmp_path, with_test=False)` - no test file at all at commit A - and asserts test_copied_from_head is True and (at_previous, at_head) == ('fail', 'pass'). The only difference between the passing case and my failing one is whether the file already existed.

Its own docstring claims the covered case is 'the commonest shape: fix and regression test land together'. That is right about the shape and wrong about the file: appending to tests/test_x.py is at least as common as creating it. This range is the proof - tests/test_code_drift.py gained 3 tests, tests/test_gate.py 2, tests/test_stop_hook.py 2, tests/test_harness.py 2, tests/test_validate.py 2, all appended to files that already existed.

Fails silent, not loud: `error` is not `fail`, so _apply_verification (harness.py:443) takes neither the refusal branch nor the fix_verified branch. The finding resolves normally with no verification, and nothing in the report says the check was attempted and could not conclude.

The consequence is the exact metric the feature was built for - harness.py's own module docstring cites '95 of 110 Sales findings undecided, no precision rate publishable'. fix_verified is what feeds outcomes.json, so under-verification keeps the track record unpublishable while looking like it is working.

root_cause.symptom: a genuinely fixed defect whose regression test was appended to an existing test file reports at_previous 'error' and never earns fix_verified
root_cause.mechanism: the counterfactual is constructed at file granularity while the thing that must travel back to the old commit is a test FUNCTION; `if not dst.exists()` reads presence of the file as presence of the test
root_cause.origin: e71121a (v0.53.0) in this range, along with the whole verification feature; the guarding test was written for the with_test=False shape and the file-exists shape was never constructed
root_cause.class: searched the verification path for other file-vs-symbol granularity assumptions: _scratch_checkout copies whole trees and _one_test_cmd rewrites only the interpreter, so this is the only site. It shares a parent with VERDICT-F-26 - both are the verification feature trusting a coarse proxy (a file path, an evidence string) for a precise object (a test function).

findings.title: verdict-issues dedupes on finding id alone, so a REGRESSED finding - the class the contract ranks first - is never re-filed and the run reports it as 'already filed'
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/issues.py:94 - the whole dedupe: `out.append((f, "exists" if fid in ledger else "create"))`. Membership of the id in the ledger is the only test.

src/verdict_mcp/issues.py:195 - the ledger entry DOES store the discriminator and nothing ever reads it back: `ledger[fid] = {**made, "hash": f.get("hash"), "created_at": ..., "run_number": ...}`. grep for `["hash"]` / `.get("hash")` in issues.py returns the write site only.

PROVEN by probe using the repository's own gh stub (tests/test_issues.py helpers, VERDICT_HOME pointed at a tempdir): run 1 with one open Critical finding filed issue #1 and wrote the ledger entry {"W-F-1": {"hash": "w-f-1", "number": 1, ...}}. The state was then changed to the regression shape - same id, hash 'brandnewhash', delta 'REGRESSED', new title and new evidence - and run 2 with --create produced: 'verdict-issues: created 0, 1 already filed, 0 deferred by --limit', with a total of 1 gh invocation across both runs.

The report is not just silent but wrong: the operator is told '1 already filed', which asserts the tracker is current for that finding. In the regression case the earlier issue was in all likelihood closed when the finding resolved, so the tracker holds a CLOSED issue and no open one.

agents/verdict.md §6 ranks this class above every other delta: 'REGRESSED - was resolved, is back <- rank these first, always'. The one integration that carries findings to the people who fix them is the one that drops it.
tests/test_issues.py:116 test_a_second_run_files_nothing_twice pins idempotence for the unchanged case and no test constructs a resolved-then-regressed finding, so the suite stays green over this.
Same shape, lesser cost: the ledger is also never reconciled with the tracker, so an issue a human deletes or transfers is never re-filed either. Not probed - the stub cannot express it.

root_cause.symptom: a finding that regressed after being resolved reaches the issue tracker zero times, and the CLI reports it as already filed
root_cause.mechanism: the ledger key is identity (the id, which by contract is minted once and never reused) while the question being asked is recurrence (has THIS occurrence been filed) - the stored `hash`, which is the recurrence fingerprint, is written and never compared
root_cause.origin: 32d1c41 (v0.56.0, 'findings meet the tracker - verdict-issues'), the last commit in this range; the module is new in this range and this is its first QA pass
root_cause.class: searched issues.py for other identity-vs-occurrence conflations: plan() is the only decision point and load_ledger/save_ledger are pure IO, so one site. The same conflation would appear in any future 'close the issue when the finding resolves' feature, which the module docstring explicitly defers.

findings.title: Diff coverage is measured in-process only, so code exercised by subprocess-invoking tests is reported as 'not imported by anything the suite executed' with every changed line unexercised - a false measured claim, and a cry-wolf risk for the new pass-refusal rule
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:563-564 writes the coverage config the run uses: `[run] dynamic_context = test_function, relative_files = True, data_file = ...` and `[json] show_contexts = True`. There is no `concurrency`, no `parallel`, and no COVERAGE_PROCESS_START - grep for all three across src/ returns nothing. coverage.py therefore records only the pytest process.

LIVE FALSE CLAIM THIS RUN: facts.json coverage.per_file['src/verdict_mcp/issues.py'] = {"changed": 217, "measured": 217, "executed": 0, "note": "not imported by anything the suite executed"} - while tests/test_issues.py contains 9 tests that execute exactly that file, via tests/test_issues.py:74 `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ISSUES), "widget", "--gh-cmd", ...])`. All 9 passed in this run's suite gate.

Same for the hooks: hooks/enforce_run_contract.py (22 changed lines, executed 0) and hooks/report_open_findings.py (5 changed lines, executed 0) carry the same note, and tests/test_stop_hook.py:26 runs them the same way - `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HOOK)], input=...)`.
244 of this run's 1125 changed lines - 22% - are misreported as unexercised on that basis, which is why the headline reads 63% rather than a number that reflects what the suite actually ran.

The renderer states it as fact in the report: harness.py:1634-1640 emits `  - <path>: unexercised lines <ranges> (<note>)` for every per-file entry with unexercised_ranges, so 'src/verdict_mcp/issues.py: unexercised lines ... (not imported by anything the suite executed)' is written into the shipped artifact.

The exactness claim is explicit and is what makes this a defect rather than a known limit - harness.py:476-478: 'Per-test attribution is a lower bound (a tracer may record a line under one context and skip it under the next); "executed by any test" is exact, and that is what the gate is built on.' It is not exact for subprocess-executed code.

LATENT: src/verdict_mcp/validate.py:267-281 (_unexercised_diff, new in this range) refuses an unqualified `pass` when changed_lines > 0 and changed_lines_executed == 0. A range confined to CLI or hook code - entirely plausible in this repo, which tests both by subprocess - measures a true zero and gets its correct `pass` refused. It did not fire this run only because the range also touched in-process code (705/1125).
This project's own profile names the shape: the plugin is a CLI plus hooks, so subprocess testing is the idiom here rather than an exception.

root_cause.symptom: the newest 217-line module in the range, with 9 dedicated passing tests, is reported in the state and the report as executed by nothing
root_cause.mechanism: coverage.py traces only the process it starts unless subprocess support is configured; the harness generates its own rc file and omits it, and the fallback branch at harness.py:602-608 then treats 'coverage never saw this file' as 'no test executed these lines', which are different statements
root_cause.origin: 6e6a859 (v0.54.0) in this range introduced _diff_coverage and the generated rc together
root_cause.class: swept the repo for the affected shape rather than the affected file: `grep -n 'subprocess.run(\[sys.executable' tests/` names test_issues.py, test_stop_hook.py and the gate/hook tests - so every CLI and hook surface in this project is measured this way, and every one of them will read as unexercised whenever its lines change. This is a class, not an instance.

findings.title: The VERDICT_STRICT bash guard reads '>' and sed expressions inside quoted strings as output redirection and resolves the phantom target against the checkout, blocking read-only QA commands
evidence: RE-PROVEN three more times this session, on three read-only commands, with the checkout unmodified throughout. (1) `python3 -c` whose source contained `if len(s)>1500:` - refused: "output redirection targets '<checkout>/1500:'". findings.title: The report's fix-verification line counts the agent's own fix_verified claim inside a block sourced from harness measurements, so a finding the harness measured as error/error is published as '1 verified'
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:1616-1623 - the block is selected by measurement (`measured = [f for f in findings if isinstance(f.get("verification"), dict)]`) and then counted by claim (`verified = sum(1 for f in measured if f.get("fix_verified") is True and f.get("delta") == "RESOLVED")`). `fix_verified` is the agent's judgment field; `verification` is the harness's measurement. One line mixes them.

LIVE IN THIS RUN'S OWN REPORT: .qa/reports/2026-09-02-delta.md renders 'Fix verification: 1 verified - 0 refused (cited test still fails at HEAD) - 0 measured but not verifiable'. The harness produced exactly one verification record this run, for VERDICT-F-20, and it reads at_previous 'error', at_head 'error', summary 'ERROR: file or directory not found: t.py::new'. The harness verified nothing. The '1' is my own fix_verified flag on F-20.

The arithmetic then empties the bucket that would have shown it: `len(measured) - verified - refused` = 1 - 1 - 0 = 0, so 'measured but not verifiable' reads zero on a run whose only measurement was unusable. The error case is not merely uncounted, it is displaced into the success count.

Independent of VERDICT-F-26, which supplied the bad id here: even with a correctly chosen test, a record of pass-at-both-commits (which harness.py:358-361 documents as verifying nothing) plus an agent-set fix_verified would render identically as 'verified'.

agents/verdict.md §9 draws the line this display erases: 'You never set the outcome ... Marking your own work correct is the one thing a tester must never be able to do', with fix_verified as the single field the agent may set - and it costs a demonstration the agent cites, not one the harness ran.

root_cause.symptom: a run whose only harness verification errored at both commits publishes 'Fix verification: 1 verified'
root_cause.mechanism: the set is chosen by the presence of a measurement and the count is taken from a judgment field on the same finding; nothing in the count consults the measurement's own at_previous/at_head result
root_cause.origin: e71121a (v0.53.0) in this range, which added both the measurement and this renderer
root_cause.class: searched the renderer for other counts that cross the measurement/judgment boundary: the gate table, the test-id ledger and the diff-coverage block all read facts-derived fields only. This is the single site - but it is the one place in the report where the two are adjacent, which is why it is also the easiest to misread.
